hook: A $29.94 showerhead fixed my weak pressure in 5 minutes

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up shot of a dribbling factory showerhead over a bathtub, weak stream, bathroom lighting, slightly disappointed framing
scenes.voiceover: I thought my shower was broken. It wasn't.

scenes.visual_prompt: Graphic overlay of a water flow regulation chart showing a 2.5 GPM federal cap over a plumbing diagram
scenes.voiceover: Every showerhead sold in the US is capped at 2.5 gallons a minute by federal law — some states go even lower.

scenes.visual_prompt: Unboxing shot of the AquaCare handheld showerhead box, price sticker overlay reading $29.94
scenes.voiceover: This one has 50,191 ratings and still holds a 4.5-star average — that's not a number you fake.

scenes.visual_prompt: Macro shot of the handheld wand cycling through spray modes, water hitting a tiled wall in slow motion
scenes.voiceover: Eight spray settings on the wand, plus a separate two-mode power wash.

scenes.visual_prompt: Time-lapse hands unscrewing old showerhead, wrapping thread tape clockwise, screwing on new bracket, stopwatch graphic counting up in corner
scenes.on_screen_text: No tools. No plumber. Under 5 minutes.
scenes.voiceover: Unscrew the old head, wrap the tape clockwise, screw on the new one — that's the entire job.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of a strong water stream hitting shoulders in the shower, steam, satisfied expression
scenes.voiceover: It's not making new pressure — it's stopping the pressure you already pay for from going to waste.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final product shot with price tag sticker and swipe-up link graphic
scenes.voiceover: Thirty bucks to test it is cheaper than one plumber visit.

caption: My shower wasn't broken — it was regulated. Swapped the $29.94 AquaCare handheld in under 5 minutes and the pressure difference is the whole post. Full breakdown + link in bio.
